---
title: "Installing packages"
date: 2026-09-28
---

Since 2026-09-28, `bioconductor.org` is served by the new stack: a Cloudflare Worker in front
of a copy of the full repository in R2 (see the [overview](index.qmd) for the design). **There
is nothing to change on your side.** `BiocManager::install()` reads the same URLs it always
has, and gets the same packages, tarballs and checksums, because the new stack still mirrors
the legacy build output hourly and checks it against the source weekly.

```r
BiocManager::install("GEOquery")
```

Checked on the day of the switch: `BiocManager::install()` against `bioconductor.org` passes
for release (3.23) and devel (3.24), from reading `config.yaml` through `PACKAGES` to
installing and loading a package.

## Is my install coming from the new stack?

Any response from `bioconductor.org` now carries `server: cloudflare` and no
`via: … cloudfront` header:

```sh
curl -sI https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/src/contrib/PACKAGES | grep -i -e '^server' -e '^via'
```

## What to expect

- **Same URLs, same content.** Landing pages, vignettes, archives and old releases all live at
  the addresses they always had.
- **Smaller downloads.** Everything is compressed, including the repository indexes R reads
  on every install: `PACKAGES` goes over the wire at about a quarter of its size.
- **Package updates appear within about an hour** of being published, as before.

## Reporting problems

An install that fails, a checksum mismatch, a slow or missing file, a page that renders
wrong: all worth reporting, however small. File a
[bioc-edge issue](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-edge/issues) with the R output and, if
possible, the failing URL, or email Sean Davis
([seandavi@gmail.com](mailto:seandavi@gmail.com)).
